game.title: Working title of the game. Do not translate until a final name is chosen.
hud.language: Button label. {language} is the language's own name (for example 'Русский') and is not translated.
confirm.newDungeon.yes: Destructive action button. Keep it short: it sits next to another button on a phone screen.
error.body: 'Last stop' means the last time the hero finished walking; that is when the game saves.
hud.health: Shown under the health bar and read by screen readers.
hud.monsters: {count} is the number of living monsters in the dungeon. The =0 form is a short victory message.
death.title: Heading of the defeat screen. Solemn, not jokey.
death.respawn: Button that brings the hero back to life at the dungeon entrance.
hud.hint: Controls summary. WASD, I and Space are physical keys and stay as they are in every language.
inventory.stack: An item name followed by how many there are, for example 'Leather × 3'.
inventory.better: Short tag next to a bag item that has higher numbers than the one currently worn.
grade.d: Equipment tier. The letter D is part of the game's terminology and is not translated.
log.picked: {item} is the item name in its dictionary form (nominative). Phrase the message so that form fits.
item.leather: All item.* names: dictionary form, capitalised as a title in English, sentence case in Russian.
hud.xp: Follows the level after a dot on the same line ('Level 3 · experience 40 of 260'), so it starts with a lower-case letter.
hud.xpMax: Shown in place of hud.xp at the last level; same position, lower-case start.
hud.dungeonLevel: How strong the monsters of the current dungeon are. Followed by the monster count on the same line.
skills.cooldown: Shown on a small skill button. {seconds} is whole seconds; 's' is the abbreviation for seconds.
skills.locked: Shown on a skill button the hero cannot use yet. Keep it very short.
skillInfo.heavyBlow: All skillInfo.* texts are tooltips: one sentence saying what the skill does, no numbers.
quick.on: State of the weapon-charges switch on a small button, followed by how many charges are left. Abbreviate if needed.
inventory.use: Button next to a potion in the bag.
shop.buyMany: Button that buys several at once; {count} is 10 or 100.
shop.noValue: Shown instead of a price next to a bag item the merchant refuses to buy.
shop.prompt: Appears when the hero stands next to the merchant. T is a physical key.
log.noneLeft: {item} is a potion name in dictionary form. Phrase the message so that form fits.
item.chargePlain: A consumable that strengthens weapon blows. The grade in brackets says which weapons it fits.
